section.title: The algebra of derivatives
section.p: Some ways of building functions are gentle. Multiplying by a constant, adding two functions, and subtracting two functions do not create any hidden interaction. Their derivatives behave exactly as we hope.
This is the first algebra of derivatives.

subsection.title: Constants disappear
subsection.p: Adding a constant shifts a graph up or down. It does not change slope.
For example, compare f(x)=x^2 and g(x)=x^2+5.
The graph of g is the graph of f shifted upward by 5. The two graphs have the same tangent slopes at corresponding x-values.
This is not a new rule. It is the sum rule together with \frac{d}{dx}(C)=0.

statement.p: The derivative records change, so it forgets vertical shifts.

subsection.title: Derivatives of polynomials
subsection.p: A polynomial is built from powers of x, constants, constant multiples, and sums. The rules above therefore give the derivative of every polynomial.
